title: Quotations for Chapter 6 (Mesopotamia and Egypt: temples, palaces and accounts): the Code of Hammurabi in King's translation and the Louvre's notice of the stele, the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary on interest, units, prices and the mīšarum edicts, Visible Language on the earliest writing and the Old Assyrian merchants, Teeter on the date of Ramesses III, Temin on Babylonian prices, Erman on payments, prices and strikes in New Kingdom Egypt, and Smith, Jevons, Menger and Mitchell Innes on the origin of money
source: L. W. King (1910, Avalon Project); Musée du Louvre; CAD vols. K (1971), M/2 (1977), Ṣ (1962), Š/3 (1992); C. Woods (ed., 2010); E. Teeter (2024); P. Temin (2003); A. Erman (1894, trans. Tirard); A. Smith (1776); W. S. Jevons (1875); C. Menger (1892, trans. Foley); A. Mitchell Innes (1913)
series: id, dynasty (place), year (negative for BC; approximate where year_note names a period), year_note, value (numbers in the quotation, ';'-separated), unit, numeral (unused), file (key of 'sources'), juan (location in the document), quote (verbatim, as in the document's text layer), note
license: Quotations for criticism and teaching, each with its source. King's translation (1910), Erman (1894), Smith (1776), Jevons (1875), Menger (1892) and Mitchell Innes (1913) are in the public domain. The Chicago Assyrian Dictionary, Visible Language and Chicago on the Nile are published as free PDFs by the University of Chicago's Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures (copyright the University of Chicago); Temin (2003) is an MIT working paper on DSpace@MIT; the Louvre's notice is quoted for the object's date, find-spot, material and size. Only short passages are quoted. Several of the PDFs are scans with a text layer; where that layer misreads a character the quotation keeps its reading and the note gives the printed form.
